label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:17:48Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17 seconds before the alert. The naive handler books every Kafka message it reads and does not skip event_ids it has already posted. The provider resends a webhook until it is acknowledged, and webhook-receiver queues each copy. So provider-events can hold the same event at several offsets, which is normal at-least-once delivery. The naive handler posted each copy, and 7 events were booked 2 or 3 times. The extra postings add up to exactly the $461.00 the ledger is ahead: $37.09 + $63.10 + $44.44 + $18.27 + $58.79 + 2 × $131.93 = $485.55 of extra payments, less $24.55 for the refund evt_000288 that was booked twice. The ledger stays balanced, because each duplicate is a full double-entry transaction. Payments and refunds still match the provider, so only the ledger is wrong.

evidence.shows: I re-ran the money check and it confirms the alert. posted_exactly_once fails with 7 events posted 2 or 3 times (evt_000308 three times). matches_provider is off by +$461.00. ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider pass.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:17:48Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. It is the only change after the stack came up at 16:16:21Z.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 ($131.93) three times, from offsets 100, 101 and 103 of partition 0, between 16:18:02 and 16:18:03. That is after the deploy.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times at those same offsets. The provider redelivered the event, so the topic held three copies.
evt_000251 was posted twice, from offsets 73 and 76 of partition 2, at 16:17:48.9 and 16:17:49.5, right after the naive-handler container started.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the handler it ran before the 16:17:48 deploy, presumably one that dedupes on event_id, so new redeliveries are not booked again. The rollback repairs nothing already booked. Afterwards, reverse the duplicate transactions with a reviewed data repair: 255, 265, 272, 273, 297, the extra postings of evt_000298 and two of evt_000308. Then re-run the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and ledger posting is delayed until it catches up from its committed offset. payment-confirmer, payments-api and webhook-receiver are not affected. If the previous handler is also wrong, ledger postings could still be bad. The ledger also stays $461.00 wrong until the data repair is done.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter). That restores the present behavior. Do it only to undo a worse failure, because it brings the double-booking back.
